sentences.text: Welcome to the Everyday English podcast series.
I'm Emily, and today we're going to learn how to speak English in a bookstore.
A bookstore is a wonderful place where you can discover new stories, learn new things, and find the perfect book for yourself or as a gift.
But what if you don't know how to ask for a book in English?
How do you find the right section?
How do you ask for recommendations or check for discounts?
Don't worry.
Entering the bookstore and asking for help.
When you enter a bookstore, you may want to browse freely, but sometimes you need help from the staff to find a book or section.
Useful English phrases for asking for help.
Excuse me, do you have this book?
Where can I find books about history, science, travel?
Can you recommend a good book?
Do you have this book in stock?
Where is the fiction non -fiction children section?
Example dialogue.
Excuse me, do you have Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone?
Let me check.
Yes, we have it in the fiction section.
Great.
Where is the fiction section?
It's on the second shelf to your right.
Tip.
If you don't know the exact book title, you can describe it by saying, I am looking for a book about space exploration.
Can you recommend one?
Asking about prices and discounts.
If you find a book you like, you may want to ask about the price or any discounts.
Useful phrases for prices and discounts.
How much does this book cost?
Is there a discount on this book?
Do you have any special offers?
Do you offer student discounts?
Is there a sale section?
Example dialogue.
How much does this book cost?
Is there a discount?
Yes, we have a 10 % discount for students.
Tip.
Some bookstores offer loyalty cards where you can collect points and get future discounts.
Checking availability and ordering books.
Sometimes the book you want is out of stock.
In this case, you can ask to order it or check if they have other additions.
Useful phrases for checking availability.
Do you have this book in stock?
Can I order this book?
How long will it take to arrive?
Can I reserve a copy?
Do you have this book in hardcover paperback?
Example dialogue.
Do you have the great Gatsby in stock?
Sorry, it's currently sold out.
Can I order a copy?
Yes, we can order it for you.
It will arrive in five days.
Tip.
If you don't mind reading on a screen, you can ask, do you have this book as an e -book?
Finding a book for a gift.
Bookstores are also great places to find gifts for friends and family.
If you don't know what to choose, you can ask the staff for recommendations.
Useful phrases for buying a book as a gift.
I want to buy a book as a gift.
Can you recommend one?
Do you have books for children, teenagers?
Is there a special edition of this book?
Do you have books with illustrations?
Can you gift wrap this book?
Example dialogue.
I want to buy a book for my friend.
Can you recommend one?
Sure.
What does your friend like?
Fiction, history, or maybe self -improvement books.
He likes science fiction.
Then I recommend Dune by Frank Herbert.
It's a great book.
Tip.
Some bookstores offer free gift wrapping services.
Paying for your books.
Once you have chosen your books, you need to go to the cashier to pay.
Useful phrases for paying.
Can I pay by card?
Do you accept cash?
Can I get a receipt?
Do you have a return policy?
Can I exchange this book if needed?
Example dialogue.
Can I pay by card?
Yes, we accept credit and debit cards.
Great.
Also, can you gift wrap this book?
Of course.
It will take just a moment.
Tip.
Keep your receipt in case you want to return or exchange the book later.
Enjoying the bookstore experience.
Many bookstores have a cafe where you can relax and read your new book.
If you want to sit and enjoy a cup of coffee, here's what you can say.
Useful phrases for a bookstore cafe.
Can I sit here and read?
Do you have a reading area?
Can I buy a coffee and read my book here?
Is this book available to read before buying?
Tip.
Some bookstores allow you to read before buying while others prefer customers to buy the books first.
That's it for today's episode.
Now you know how to speak English in a bookstore.
We covered asking for help, finding books, asking about prices and discounts, ordering a book, buying a book as a gift, paying at the cashier, enjoying a bookstore cafe.
Next time you visit a bookstore, try using these phrases.
Thank you for listening and see you in the next episode.
